title: Local Data and Backup
summary: Your ledger lives on this device only - nothing syncs between devices or employees, and the only copies that exist anywhere else are the ones you export or the device backups you already make.

sections.heading: Where your records live
paragraphs: Cores, vendors, bins, return batches, event history, photos, scanned receipts, and your settings are stored in the app's own storage inside its container on this device.
That is the working copy, and it is the only copy the app keeps.

sections.heading: Nothing syncs
paragraphs: CoreCredit has no account, no cloud sync, and no shared workspace. Two devices running the app keep two separate ledgers that never see each other.
There is no way for two employees to work in the same ledger through the app. If several people need the same information, the practical answer today is one shared device, or exports you send them.
A device backup made by Apple is not sync. Restoring one device from another device's backup is an Apple feature, not a CoreCredit one.

sections.heading: Making your own copy
paragraphs: Settings, then Data and export, can produce a spreadsheet export of the ledger (CSV), a printable ledger document (PDF), and a portable backup file (JSON) that contains the whole ledger.
Each file is generated on the device and then handed to the share sheet, where you decide where it goes - Files, mail, a note app, a computer, or a printer.
Make a backup before anything risky: erasing the app's data, replacing a device, or handing the device to someone else.

sections.heading: Reading a backup back in
paragraphs: CoreCredit can restore a backup file it wrote. Data & export has a Restore from backup action that reads a .json backup, checks it, shows you exactly what it contains, and asks you to confirm before anything changes.

A restore REPLACES everything currently on this device. It is not a merge. Cores, vendors, bins, returns, the event history, and the shop profile in the file take the place of what is on the device now. There is no undo.

The whole file is read and checked before a single existing record is removed. If the file is empty, damaged, not a CoreCredit backup, or was written by a newer version of the app than the one you are running, the restore stops and your existing ledger is left exactly as it was.

One thing a backup does not carry: EVIDENCE PHOTOS. The backup file is a text file of your records - part names, numbers, references, amounts, dates, statuses, and the event history. The photographs you attached to cores are not in it, and a restore cannot bring them back. Keep photos through your device backup, which does include them.
For the same reason, a restore is a way to move a ledger to a replacement device or to recover from a mistake - not a substitute for the device backup Apple already makes.

sections.heading: Generated files are temporary
paragraphs: Exports and bin tags are written into the app's caches folder, and files older than about a day are swept away automatically to keep the app from hoarding copies of your ledger.
That sweep only ever touches files the app itself generated. A file you have already shared or saved elsewhere is untouched by it.

sections.heading: Photos and evidence
paragraphs: Photos you attach to a core - the part, the box, the invoice, the credit memo - are stored with that core in the app's own storage, not in your photo library.
They are included in a dispute packet only when you generate one, and that packet goes only where you send it.

sections.heading: Erasing everything
paragraphs: The Erase control on the Data and export screen removes the shop's records from this device and clears the reminders that were queued for them.
It cannot reach files you have already exported and sent elsewhere, and it cannot reach a device backup you have already made.
Deleting the app removes its container, and everything in it, from the device.

sections.heading: If the device is lost, broken, or replaced
paragraphs: The developer holds no copy of your records and cannot recover them. There is no server to recover them from.
What can bring the information back is your own material: the exports you saved, and the iCloud or computer backup of the device itself, restored through Apple in the normal way.

sections.heading: Keeping the ledger worth trusting
paragraphs: The ledger is only as accurate as what was typed or scanned into it. Check recognised text, barcode results, amounts, deadlines, and credit figures against the paperwork.
Where the app and an invoice or credit memo disagree, the paperwork is the record that counts.

sections.heading: Questions
paragraphs: Questions about your data, an export, or a restore go to support@idlery.com.
The support page is at https://corecredit.idlery.com/support.
